rules.statement: Validate every requested scope at both the authorization endpoint and the token endpoint against the client's resolved allowed-scope set, and reject any scope outside it with the `invalid_scope` error.
rules.why: A client may only obtain the scopes it is entitled to; the entitlement model does nothing unless the runtime checks it on every request path.
rules.check: Look for authorization or token request validators that skip scope validation, validate on only one endpoint, return an error code other than `invalid_scope` for unauthorized scopes, or quietly drop unauthorized scopes instead of rejecting the request.

rules.statement: Compare OAuth scope tokens case-sensitively, using ordinal comparison, never case-insensitive or culture-aware comparison.
rules.why: RFC 6749 defines scope tokens as case-sensitive strings.
rules.check: Look for scope sets or comparisons that use `StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`, `ToLower`/`ToUpper` normalization, `InvariantCultureIgnoreCase`, or culture-sensitive equality on scope values.

rules.statement: When computing a client's allowed scopes from stored grants, intersect the granted scopes with the scopes the resource currently defines at read time, so a scope that is no longer defined is ignored even if a grant still lists it.
rules.why: Without the read-time intersection, a scope removed from an API stays in old grants and keeps being honored until every grant is rewritten. Intersecting at read time keeps the resource server authoritative at all times.
rules.check: Look for allowed-scope resolution that returns a grant's stored scope list as-is, without intersecting it with the resource's current scope definitions, or that relies only on validation when the grant is written.

rules.statement: Build the discovery document's `scopes_supported` metadata from the authoritative resource and scope catalog (the distinct scopes of enabled resources). Don't add a separately configured setting or a hard-coded list for it.
rules.why: A second flat list of allowed scopes is a second source of truth that drifts from the resource/grant model.
rules.check: Look for a configurable setting, option, or hard-coded scope list that feeds discovery `scopes_supported` or acts as a ceiling during request validation alongside the resource/grant model.
